answer: Each agent must post a bond that is slashed if its signed actions are later shown to violate the market’s rules, while rewards accrue only after a long, public history of useful work. A newcomer cannot echo trusted agents’ reputations: each identity starts with its own bond and track record. This makes a sybil swarm expensive, since the attacker must lock capital in every account and keep each one behaving over time; karst-like hidden channels or marble-bright profile details do not substitute for either.
